identity.name: LANDMARK GLOBAL LEARNING LIMIT
identity.industry: Education / International Student Advisory & Campus Expansion

summary.oneLiner: H1FY26 revenue declined due to deferred enrollments and tighter global visa policies, but management is aggressively expanding into Dubai and Paris campuses with near-term licensing imminent, positioning for revenue recovery and margin expansion in FY27-28.

one-line thesis: H1FY26 revenue declined due to deferred enrollments and tighter global visa policies, but management is aggressively expanding into Dubai and Paris campuses with near-term licensing imminent, positioning for revenue recovery and margin expansion in FY27-28.
financial scorecard: Revenue: -6% YoY (INR15.6cr vs INR16.6cr); EBITDA: -42% YoY (INR74L vs INR128L); PAT (reported): -38% YoY (INR2.1cr vs INR3.4cr); PAT (normalized): same; order book: not disclosed; net debt: not disclosed - one-off: higher branch expansion and fair sponsorship costs compressed margins
guidance: Revenue growth: FY26 flat vs FY25; FY27 target INR80-90cr; Margin: FY27 PAT margin target 20-25%; Order inflow: not specified; Capex/commissioning: Dubai campus to launch Q4FY26, Paris campus Q1FY27, asset-light (rental model)
segment / subsidiary detail: Canada: ~70% of revenue; UK and Germany: growing from <10% to significant share; Revenue model: primarily commissions from universities; minimal student fees
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Bangladesh (live), Africa, Nepal, Pakistan; Dubai and Paris campuses to enable direct institutional partnerships and third-party agent sourcing; potential to monetize curriculum licensing
margins & cost dynamics: Margin compression due to fixed cost absorption on lower revenue + aggressive branch expansion (5 new branches) + sponsorship of international education fairs (APAIE, PAL, ICEF); Opex per campus not quantified but asset-light
capex / expansion: Asset-light model; no major CAPEX; costs are operating expenses (rent, staffing, curriculum setup); Dubai and Paris campuses expected to break even within first year
capital allocation: Prioritizing geographic expansion (Dubai, Paris, Africa, Nepal, Pakistan) over buybacks or debt reduction; reinvesting in brand building and campus setup
risks & watch-items: Further visa policy tightening in key markets (Canada, UK, Germany); delay in Dubai/Paris licensing; slower-than-expected student conversion post-campuses launch; reliance on university commissions; macroeconomic headwinds affecting education loans
management quality / tone: Cautious on current H1FY26 performance but highly confident and excited about near-term campus launches; framing slowdown as temporary, not structural; strong emphasis on brand repositioning from 'immigration' to 'global education'
non-obvious takeaways: Dubai campus licensing is imminent (expected within 2 weeks of call date); management has hired a global strategy director with 26+ years’ experience specifically to execute this expansion; campus model allows third-party agent sourcing, reducing dependency on own recruitment
